title: He Is Twenty-Three, Captaining India A, and Already the Vice-Captain of the Senior T20I Team.
excerpt: Tilak Varma's appointment as vice-captain for the Ireland and England T20I tours is no accident. In Dambulla, he is auditioning for something bigger.
body:
On Monday morning in Dambulla, Tilak Varma won the toss for India A against Sri Lanka A and chose to bat. It was the kind of straightforward decision that gets forgotten by lunch. But the context around it matters far more than the call itself.

Three days earlier, the BCCI announced that Varma would serve as Shreyas Iyer's vice-captain for India's upcoming T20I tours to Ireland and England, starting June 26. The appointment displaced Axar Patel, whose captaincy stints in the IPL had apparently failed to convince the selectors. In Tilak, the board sees something they have been looking for since Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli walked away from T20 internationals: a young batter who can lead.

## Dambulla as an Audition

The Tri-Nation A series in Sri Lanka — featuring India A, Sri Lanka A, and Afghanistan A — is not a glamorous assignment. The matches are broadcast on a single network, the stadiums are half-empty, and the stakes appear low. But for Indian cricket's leadership pipeline, the series is one of the most important assignments of the summer.

India A's playing XI for the opening match read like a roster of futures: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old IPL Orange Cap winner, opening the innings; Prabhsimran Singh keeping wicket; Priyansh Arya at number three; Ruturaj Gaikwad, who replaced the injured Riyan Parag, batting at four. Varma slotted himself at five and let the youngsters set the tone.

Sooryavanshi fell cheaply — dismissed for 14 — and the innings briefly wobbled before Gaikwad steadied it with a measured fifty. Varma himself contributed a brisk knock down the order, and India A posted 277 for 6, which proved more than enough against Sri Lanka A.

## A Pattern the Selectors Want

What makes Varma's candidacy interesting is not his batting record, which is solid but not yet dominant at international level. It is his composure. In 14 domestic T20 captaincy assignments for Hyderabad, he won nine. His IPL 2026 season for Mumbai Indians was uneven — 359 runs at a strike rate of 145 — but his ability to absorb pressure without visibly cracking has earned comparisons to a young Rohit Sharma.

The selectors have noticed. Rohit himself reportedly backed Varma as a future Mumbai Indians captain. The BCCI management has watched him field-set in T20s, rotate bowling changes calmly in ODIs, and manage young bowlers' confidence in tight moments. The Dambulla assignment is their way of testing whether that composure translates when the team sheet reads "captain."

## The Bigger Picture

India's T20I setup is undergoing its most significant overhaul since the 2007 World Cup generation retired. Suryakumar Yadav, who won the T20 World Cup as captain earlier this year, has been replaced by Shreyas Iyer. Shubman Gill, the Test captain, was left out entirely. The squad for Ireland and England features Sooryavanshi, Prince Yadav, and Prasidh Krishna alongside the familiar names — a signal that the management is building for 2028, not just the next series.

Varma sits at the centre of this reconstruction. At 23, he has already played nearly 50 T20Is for India. He bats in the middle order, bowls part-time spin when needed, and fields with the kind of urgency that coaches love. His elevation to vice-captain is the clearest indication yet that Indian cricket sees him as a future captain, not just a future number five.

## What Comes Next

The tri-series in Sri Lanka runs through mid-June, giving Varma three or four more matches as captain. He will then fly to Belfast, where India open their Ireland T20I series on June 26 before moving to England for five T20Is starting July 1. In those matches, he will stand next to Shreyas Iyer in the team huddle as the man entrusted with thinking about the game when the captain cannot.

For the Indian diaspora in the UK, the timing is notable. Varma's IPL performances have made him recognisable in ways that most India A captains never are. When he takes the field at Durham or Manchester alongside Iyer, he will do so as the player Indian cricket is betting on to lead the next decade — a 23-year-old from Hyderabad whose journey from Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy captain to international vice-captain took less than three years.

**India's T20I Squad for Ireland and England:** Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma (vc), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Ishan Kishan (wk), Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakravarthy, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Harshit Rana, Prasidh Krishna, Ravi Bishnoi
